speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will consider reviewing the criteria of the Silver Support Scheme so that more seniors in need of the support can be assisted; and (b) whether the criteria for the scheme can be better communicated and explained to the seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Seniors do not need to apply for Silver Support.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They are automatically assessed annually, and the payouts are directly credited into the senior's registered bank account or sent to the senior's registered address via a cheque.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Currently, all seniors who are eligible for Silver Support in any given year are automatically notified by the CPF Board in December of the preceding year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For newly eligible recipients, the notification letter contains an accompanying infographic which explains the qualifying criteria in all four vernacular languages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We also disseminate information on Silver Support through Community Centres and Silver Generation Ambassadors who are trained to explain the scheme to seniors during their house visits.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If Members have suggestions on how the Silver Support eligibility criteria can be better communicated, we are happy to take these comments on board and we are happy to look into them as well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My question is more for seniors who used to receive and depended on the payouts, and subsequently, the payouts stopped because of changes in their household income and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I understand that the CPF Board does review seniors' eligibility annually but I want to ask the Minister whether for those who used to receive and subsequently do not receive payouts, how does the CPF Board communicate this to those seniors?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: What are the reasons that are given to them – whether they used to receive for many years and then they do not receive payouts.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Should there not be a clarification as to how that happens?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Because many of the seniors depended on the payouts for some years and suddenly, it just gets removed.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: There could be some problems for them to manage their monthly expenses and so on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The CPF Board automatically reviews a senior's eligibility for Silver Support every year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The main reason for seniors becoming ineligible usually could be due to a combination of reasons.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It could be due to increases in their household monthly income per person, which is a broad indicator of the level of household support which is available to the senior.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In many of these circumstances, the senior's financial situation has actually improved.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For those seniors who no longer qualify for Silver Support in the following year, they will be notified in the preceding year – in December of the preceding year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For instance, if the senior no longer qualifies for Silver Support for 2023, they will receive notification in December 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Having said that, the CPF Board also considers appeals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: When seniors find that notwithstanding the support that has been withdrawn, they are not able to be able to transition appropriately, we are prepared to consider each appeal.
